channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Paedophile who sexually abused infant and incited rape of another child jailed
item.description: A paedophile who sexually abused an infant and incited the rape of another child has been jailed for 10-and-a-half years.

item.title: Ukraine: Ceasefire holds for its first 30 hours in occupied Oleshky
item.description: A local ceasefire in the Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky held through its first day and night, despite continued fighting between Moscow and Kyiv elsewhere. The truce, which began on Tuesday in the devastated city, is expected to remain in place until Sunday. Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: At least 30 killed in train collision on high-speed line in Spain
item.description: At least 30 people were killed after two trains collided on Spain's Madrid-Andalucía high-speed line, a spokeswoman for the Castilla-La Mancha region said.

item.title: US midterms: Slashing of food stamps in Arizona angers voters
item.description: With the US midterm elections just under a week away, the cost of living has emerged as a key campaign issue. In Arizona, many Americans are criticising the administration’s decision to slash food stamps, which has had significant consequences for the poorest. Camille Corcoran reports.

item.title: WATCH: King tides swamp homes with seawater in South Florida and California coasts
item.description: Some of the highest tides ever recorded in South Florida and California have sent surging seawater into nearby towns – flooding homes on both coasts, and triggering water rescues.

item.title: Israel: Netanyahu edges closer to a majority
item.description: The final results are expected tonight or tomorrow morning. For now, the picture is looking increasingly favourable for Benjamin Netanyahu and his bloc, but the Israeli prime minister is still short of a clear victory, as he needs 61 seats to secure a parliamentary majority. He addressed his supporters at the National Congress Centre at around 3 a.m. local time. France 24’s Clovis Casali joins us live from Jerusalem with the latest.

item.title: Spain: Local authorities confirm at least 10 dead in train accident
item.description: Two trains travelling in opposite directions have collided in southern Spain, on the route between Madrid and Seville. At least 10 deaths have been confirmed, although some media reports put the toll as high as 39. The crash brings back painful memories of a deadly train accident in Córdoba in January. The cause of the collision remains unknown. France 24 correspondent Sarah Morris joins us live from Madrid with the latest.

item.title: Israeli election: 'Wishful thinking' for pro- and anti-Netanyahu parties?
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, October 28: Papers react to the ongoing election results in Israel. Next: Macklemore's Free Palestine tour is coming to Paris. Also: antidepressants don't work the way we thought. Finally: a sneak peek into boomer divorcées' dating lives.

item.title: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu remains far from defeated
item.description: Arab-led parties appear to have made a historic showing in the Israeli election, but it’s not clear if other opponents of Netanyahu's government would form a coalition with them for a majority in the next parliament. Issues around the Palestinians and their descendants remain incredibly sensitive in Israel. France 24 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert shares further insights.

item.title: Spain: At least 10 dead in crash between 2 high-speed trains
item.description: At least ten people have died in a crash between two trains in central Spain. The crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Rail service is suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia. France 24's correspondent in Madrid Sarah Morris reports the latest.

item.title: At least 30 dead in crash between two trains in central Spain, media say
item.description: A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people on Wednesday in central Spain, according to local media. (Image credit: Juanma Jiménez)

item.title: Knife attacker shot dead by police outside Israeli embassy
item.description: A man carrying knives has been killed by police after attacking an officer outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade.

item.title: Israel: The economic challenges ahead
item.description: Questions over the future of Israel’s economy are looming in the wake of the elections. With one of the highest costs of living in the region, and defence spending continuing to rise, households are facing growing financial pressure. Caitlin Brown reports.

item.title: Israel election: There's no clear winner
item.description: The path ahead remains uncertain in the Knesset in Jerusalem, as the Central Elections Committee continues to count the votes. With more than 60% of ballots tallied, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp is narrowly ahead of the opposition, but still short of a clear majority. These are still partial results and could change, meaning no clear winner has emerged so far. Both leading candidates for the prime minister’s office traded barbs in their respective speeches after polls closed. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

item.title: Why California's election results take longer than other states
item.description: Trump continues to sow doubt in California elections and mail ballots.

item.title: Israel: Netanyahu and Eisenkot both pledge to form government
item.description: 🗳️ Both Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin #Netanyahu and rival Gadi #Eisenkot pledged to form a government as the two are projected to finish neck and neck in #Israel's critical election Tuesday. Exit polls show both blocs falling short of a parliamentary majority.

item.title: Dozens killed in high-speed train collision in central Spain
item.description: At least 30 people have been killed on Wednesday after two high-speed trains collided in Spain's central Toledo province, regional authorities said. High-speed rail services between Madrid and Andalusia have been suspended.

item.title: Senate candidates built up massive campaign war chests with out-of-state donations
item.description: In several competitive U.S. Senate contests, candidates have built healthy campaign accounts with out-of-state donations. But the messages to those donors is very different from the one back at home. (Image credit: Elijah Nouvelage)

item.title: Why many student voters have a right to choose where to register to vote
item.description: Student voters studying outside their hometown have a right to choose where they register to vote. Advocates say a Montana legal fight is a reminder of a misunderstanding of those students' rights. (Image credit: Ryan M. Kelly)

item.title: Partnerships between ICE and local police surge, report finds
item.description: The number of state and local officers working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement has doubled in size in the last eight months, according to a new report from the immigration reform advocacy group FWD.us. (Image credit: Charly Triballeau)

item.title: Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims
item.description: Congressional Democrats are working with good governance groups to create an action plan for any potential claims of election fraud. (Image credit: RYAN MURPHY)

item.title: Are you an organ donor? Here are some rule changes you may want to know
item.description: Transplant teams can talk to families about organ donation before they've decided whether to continue life-sustaining medical care for loved ones. Until now, that has been forbidden.

item.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio
item.description: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns. (Image credit: Andrea Hsu)

item.title: New teachers union president wants to steer educators away from partisan politics
item.description: NEA President Princess Moss wants to move her organization, the nation's largest labor union, toward issue-based advocacy — and away from party politics. (Image credit: The National Education Association)

item.title: French Senate debates new 'rioters pay' bill
item.description: As thousands of French businesses grapple with the fallout from recent riots, French senators are debating a new bill aimed at making not only the perpetrators but also those belonging to the same group pay for damages. The idea of "collective civil liability" divides lawmakers, with opponents saying it could potentially violate people's democratic rights to protest as some might stay clear of demonstrations for fear of being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

item.title: Zookeeper dies after leopard attack
item.description: A woman has died after being attacked by a leopard at the safari park where she spent almost her entire 40-year career.

item.title: US cruise ship ends global voyage due to fuel costs; 200 passengers lose their homes
item.description: A U.S. cruise ship on a residential world voyage has suspended its operations in Cambodia due to fuel costs, forcing hundreds of passengers to abandon their homes

item.title: Trump's cure for Republicans' midterm woes is more Trump. Will it work?
item.description: President Donald Trump wants midterm voters to imagine he's on the ballot and has seized the political spotlight in a way that makes such make-believe seem a bit more real

item.title: Republicans emphasize transgender ads, putting cultural issues over economy
item.description: Republicans have spent an estimated $183 million on television ads focused on transgender-related attacks against Democrats in the final phase of this year’s midterm elections

item.title: Federal judge rules top US prosecutor in Los Angeles isn't legally serving
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that Republican Bill Essayli is not legally serving as the top U.S. prosecutor in Los Angeles

item.title: Kylian Mbappé apologises after Mao Zedong joke
item.description: Several major Chinese companies have ended their partnerships with Kylian Mbappé after he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Mbappé has apologised, citing "a deep respect for the Chinese people and their history".

item.title: Real Madrid apologise to China over Mbappé's Mao Zedong comments
item.description: Real Madrid apologised to the Chinese people on Wednesday after star striker Kylian Mbappé sparked a furious backlash over comments referring to the founding leader of Communist China as a dictator. The club's apology came a day after Mbappé and Spain's La Liga football championship expressed regret over the comments.

item.title: UK set for calmer weather - but 'dense' fog may cause disruption
item.description: The UK is set for a period of calmer weather after three people died during storms over the weekend - but "dense" fog could cause further disruption.

item.title: US embassy worker flown out of UK before police questioning
item.description: A senior US Air Force officer was flown out of the UK before he could be questioned over allegations that he possessed child sexual abuse images, it has emerged.

item.title: Rights groups oppose UAE’s Lana Nusseibeh for UN chief over Sudan claims
item.description: Human rights groups on Tuesday urged countries to reject UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh’s bid to become United Nations secretary general citing allegations that Abu Dhabi funds Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UAE denies the accusations. Nusseibeh, 48, is seeking to become the first woman to lead the UN.

item.title: French Senate backs 'make rioters pay' bill despite rights concerns
item.description: France's Senate on Wednesday approved a bill authorising rioters to be held financially accountable for damage caused during social unrest, with penalties of up to €10,000 and possible welfare benefit seizures. Rights groups warn the legislation could undermine the public's fundamental right to protest.

item.title: EPA response to 2023 Ohio train derailment will be investigated by agency watchdog
item.description: The Environmental Protection Agency’s response to the disastrous 2023 East Palestine train derailment will be investigated after dozens of residents of the small town on the Ohio-Pennsylvania and Vice President JD Vance requested the review

item.title: King Charles confronts calls for slavery apology during Caribbean tour
item.description: King Charles III began a Caribbean tour in the Bahamas on Tuesday, acknowledging “the great suffering of the past” amid calls for an apology over slavery. The 77-year-old monarch, who is undergoing cancer treatment, will also visit Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, highlighting climate threats and attending a Commonwealth summit with Queen Camilla.

item.title: Israel election: Netanyahu and Eisenkot battle to form government after deadlock
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot on Wednesday both pledged to form a government after an election left neither bloc with a parliamentary majority. Record voter turnout followed a divisive campaign dominated by the October 7, 2023 attack, while Arab Israeli parties made significant gains.

item.title: WATCH: Harry Kane is the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or & more
item.description: Harry Kane and Alèxia Putellas win the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards; NFL recap: Dallas Cowboys defeat the Philadelphia Eagles; Sarah J. Maas releases sixth book of 'A Court of Thorns and Roses' series

item.title: Israel: First exit polls show no clear winner, Arab parties make gains
item.description: Exit polls on Tuesday showed that the opposition bloc led by Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot gained a narrow edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud bloc in the Knesset. Likud, however, was projected to be the largest single party in the Israeli parliament.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro flies from Argentina after Brazil election defeat
item.description: Argentina has said Flavio Bolsonaro entered the country before boarding a private flight to Ecuador on Tuesday after losing Brazil's presidential election.

item.title: Bibi's moment of truth: Israel votes in first general election since October 7 attacks
item.description: The turnout tells the tale. Israelis are casting ballots in their largest numbers in decades in the first general election since the October 7 attacks of 2023. The vote is seen as a referendum on the bloodiest day in the nation's history. But more broadly, what kind of Israel do citizens want?

item.title: FBI agents charged with lying about Hunter Biden probes accuse DOJ of 'serious abuse'
item.description: Attorneys for a former FBI agent charged with lying to Congress about the probe into Hunter Biden's laptop computer call the charges "a serious abuse."

item.title: CDC's deputy director resigns after being hired in April
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's deputy director and chief medical officer has resigned, the agency said in a statement on Tuesday.

item.description: The FBI confirmed the search to ABC News.

item.description: The parents of Alex Pretti demanded transparent from the Department of Justice in regards to their son's killing by federal agents on January 24th.

item.description: The filmmaker and ski mountaineer discuss National Geographic's "Everest: The Other Side," documenting a daring climb up Mount Everest's north face and a ski descent.

item.title: WATCH: Widow of man killed on George Washington Bridge demands justice
item.description: Patricia Irvine's husband was fatally shot in an alleged road-rage incident on the upper deck of New York's George Washington Bridge.

item.description: At least 62 people have been killed after an attack in northeastern Nigeria, the country's emergency agency said.

item.description: Police in Germany say stormy weather caused the ship to drift toward the dock. No one was hurt.

item.description: Republicans currently hold majorities in the House and Senate. How many seats must Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer flip to seize control of Congress?

item.description: A Florida youth soccer organizer called police this past weekend to remove the parents of a 3-year-old boy who the organizer said were being disruptive.

item.title: Hundreds of troops sent to deal with anti-immigration protests
item.description: More than 500 soldiers have been sent to deal with anti-migrant protests in South Africa, the country's government has said.

item.description: As both parties prepare for the final leg of the campaign, here are some of the most closely watched Senate races.

item.description: French footballer Kylian Mbappe has apologised for an "ill-judged" remark about Mao Zedong after being dropped by Chinese brands.

item.title: Ebola cases in DRC surpass 10,000 as nurse treating patients is killed by machete-wielding mob
item.description: The number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has surpassed 10,000, government data showed, as fears that the epidemic could spread to more African countries grow.

item.description: Marilyn Hampton was a custodian in the Aubrey School District in Denton County, Texas, who made her mark over the course of four decades.

item.description: A total of 184 people set a world record, decked out in pointed hats and witches’ cloaks, 400 feet up on the Orlando Eye.

item.title: WATCH: Three ‘hobbits’ dive for hours to find lost ring, return it 1,000 miles away
item.description: In a real-life "Lord of the Rings" quest, three friends and self-proclaimed “hobbits” roped themselves to boulders and spent hours diving into a Tuscan river to find a stranger’s lost wedding ring.
